assessment.calibration_basis: Held at the scorecard's cal_p/p_engine (0.7674, rounded to 0.77) rather than moving toward either bound: cms_p is 0.8491 and matches the real-time risk_score of 0.87, and a second in-person transaction in the same 48h window and same modal region (3514573, cms_p 0.72) corroborates the flagged transaction rather than looking like isolated model noise. Two independent families support fraud - case-memory (cms_p/cal_p plus 18 prior confirmed_fraud closed cases on this exact card, 8 of them account_takeover confirmed inside this same modal region) and history (the neighboring high-score transaction). Countervailing history evidence - amount within baseline, region is modal/home, and a same-place/product recurrence at this amount - keeps probability below 0.85 rather than pushing it higher, and the recurring-charge check's gap-CV (0.60) narrowly fails the R7 exemption, so it tempers but does not clear the score.

evidence.claim: case_context shows the flagged transaction 3514948 ($111.92, in_person, product W, billing region 264.0, 2016-12-05 00:46:14) scored cms_p 0.8491 (calibrated 0.7674) against a real-time risk_score of 0.87.

episode_candidates over the 48h window before opening shows a second in-person transaction in the same region, 3514573 ($36.97, 2016-12-04 22:40:36, about 2.1 hours before the flagged transaction), scoring cms_p 0.72 - both are anomalous against the rest of the 7-day chain, which mostly scores well under cms_p 0.05.

prior_cases_for_customer lists 18 prior confirmed_fraud closed cases on card C09933-K2 (account_takeover and out_of_region_use patterns, most recent CC-5521 opened 2016-10-31), making this a card with a repeat-fraud history rather than a clean baseline.

8 of those prior confirmed cases (CC-5521, CC-4787, CC-4597, CC-4455, CC-3136, CC-2834) carry pattern account_takeover and were confirmed as all-in-person fraud inside this same modal region (264.0), which by the labeling convention is this card's established fraud shape, so an in-region in-person purchase here is not automatically ordinary use.

region_history confirms 264.0 is the card's modal in-person region (2,224 prior purchases over 156 days, share 0.92) with continuous home activity in the surrounding 48h window (24 home vs 2 other transactions), and case_context's card_seq places the flagged transaction's amount ($111.92) between the card's prior median ($77.04) and prior maximum ($2,529.78) over 2,431 prior transactions - read together, these are the legitimacy-side facts the memory-based score has to be weighed against.

recurring_charge_check finds 5 prior purchases within 1% of $111.92, same product code W, same billing region 264.0, median gap 16.0 days but gap CV 0.60, which narrowly fails the R7 monthly-cadence exemption test (CV must be <=0.6), so this recurrence does not clear the transaction as the customer's own settled pattern.

ring_profile and shared_origin_scan show the flagged transaction carries no device record (channel in_person, device_known false) and the card's own strong device profile (LG-K450 Build/MXB48T | Android 6.0.1 | chrome 63.0 for android | 1280x720) has n_fraud_cases 0, so no shared-origin or shared-device evidence ties to this episode.
